summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (N25) proposing a research hypothesis ("assumption-kill") to test whether atomoxetine retains a working memory (WM) / attention phenotype when the norepinephrine transporter (NET/Slc6a2) is genetically knocked out or pharmacologically blocked to abolish NET-class attribution. The document is a structured research discussion — not a completed experiment — framing the claim, prior art, prediction variables, and proposed assay design. No experimental data have been generated; the key residual-under-abolish result is explicitly marked UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis Statement (N25)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (or NHP Gamo-class) WM/attention panel with an atomoxetine-alone arm, a NET genetic LOF (Slc6a2) or NET-matched blockade that abolishes NET-class attribution, and an atomoxetine-under-abolish arm: under the same condition that abolishes NET-class attribution, atomoxetine retains residual WM/attention phenotype ≥50% of atomoxetine-alone (WM/attention units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified). This is framed as an 'assumption-kill / net-insufficiency' test of the standard NET orthosteric blockade framing for atomoxetine's cognitive effects.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content: Atomoxetine WM/attention phenotypes are commonly attributed to NET orthosteric blockade. The four key prior-art references (Xu, Bymaster, Gamo, Michelson) each provide partial support (KO tool, mechanism attribution, WM phenotype, ADHD RCT) but none includes a residual-positive arm under NET abolish. The question is whether any residual atomoxetine WM/attention phenotype survives Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched blockade — i.e., whether NET blockade is necessary and sufficient for the atomoxetine cognitive phenotype. Explicitly distinguished from N15 (modafinil/DAT), N22 (tyrosine/AMPT), N23 (guanfacine/α2), and N24 (caffeine/A2A).

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Net-insufficiency assumption-kill: Atomoxetine is framed as a selective NET blocker (Bymaster: NET-selective PFC NE/DA elevation). Slc6a2/NET KO is an established genetic tool (Xu). Published WM/ADHD phenotype priors exist (Gamo PFC WM in NHP; Michelson ADHD RCT). No published head-to-head study scores residual-positive atomoxetine WM/attention under Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched blockade that abolishes NET-class attribution on the same panel. Preferred design: same-panel acute/subacute rodent (or NHP Gamo-class) WM/attention lock with atomoxetine ± Slc6a2 LOF or named NET-matched abolish condition. Optional cell/SPR/NET occupancy overlay only after abolish-verification locks residual.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four prior-art references identified:
1. PMID 10769386 (Xu, Nat Neurosci 2000, DOI 10.1038/74839): Slc6a2/NET KO mice — prolonged NE clearance, elevated extracellular NE, antidepressant-like behaviour, psychostimulant locomotor supersensitivity. KO tool prior; NO atomoxetine WM/attention residual-under-abolish arm.
2. PMID 12431845 (Bymaster, Neuropsychopharmacology 2002, DOI 10.1016/S0893-133X(02)00346-9): Atomoxetine is NET-selective; increases extracellular NE and DA in PFC. NET-mechanism attribution prior; NOT residual-under-abolish WM H2H.
3. PMID 20855046 (Gamo, JAACAP 2010, DOI 10.1016/j.jaac.2010.06.015): Atomoxetine (and MPH) enhance prefrontal WM in monkeys; benefit challenged by idazoxan (α2-antagonist) or SCH23390 (D1-antagonist). WM phenotype prior + α2/D1 downstream mediation. α2 ≠ NET — NOT a NET abolish residual/necessity test.
4. PMID 12411225 (Michelson, Am J Psychiatry 2002, DOI 10.1176/appi.ajp.159.11.1896): Once-daily atomoxetine ADHD RCT in children/adolescents. Human attention phenotype prior; NO NET-abolish residual arm.
Overall prior art status: PARTIAL — NET-mechanism attribution FOUND; residual-positive under abolish ABSENT; phenotype/tool priors FOUND.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Under NET genetic LOF (Slc6a2) or NET-matched blockade abolishing NET-class attribution, atomoxetine retains WM/attention phenotype on the same panel — OR Bymaster already proves residual under NET abolish — OR Xu/Gamo/Michelson phenotype already constitutes residual-under-abolish or genetic WM necessity-abolish H2H — OR Gamo idazoxan×ATM already is NET abolish — OR N1–N24 already settle residual atomoxetine under NET abolish.
Baseline measured: Xu (PMID 10769386) — KO tool LITERATURE without atomoxetine WM residual arm. Bymaster (PMID 12431845) — NET-mechanism attribution LITERATURE, not residual-under-abolish WM H2H. Gamo (PMID 20855046) — WM phenotype prior; α2 ≠ NET. Michelson (PMID 12411225) — phenotype prior without residual-under-abolish arm. Matched residual-positive atomoxetine under Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched block: UNKNOWN (soft-complete Q_resid_tight NON-MATCH; Q_xu_atom=0; Q_atom_net_ko=DAT-KO NON-MATCH PMID 36291693; genetic WM necessity-abolish H2H NOT FOUND). Residual ≥50% of atomoxetine-alone: PREDICTION.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. N1–N24 do not prove N25: N15 (DAT ≠ NET; Ptukha 36291693 is DAT-KO×atomoxetine NON-MATCH); N22 (AMPT catecholamine-depletion ≠ NET LOF); N23 (α2 ≠ NET; Gamo idazoxan×ATM is α2-downstream adjacent, not NET abolish); N16–N21, N24 are distinct mechanisms. Soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual gain.
2. NET-mechanism attribution FOUND (Bymaster 12431845) — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL OK, not auto-REJECT. Do not invent residual-positive H2H from mechanism literature. Xu/Gamo/Michelson phenotype ≠ residual H2H. Adjacent Yang 19387424 (Slc6a2 haplotype↔response) is pharmacogenetics not LOF residual/necessity.
3. Lock same-panel acute/subacute rodent (or NHP Gamo-class) WM/attention with atomoxetine ± Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched challenge; no dosing; NOT MB/MAOI; orthosteric_drift=false; do not burn ip_class=none; do not treat α2-downstream as NET abolish.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove same-panel contrast of residual atomoxetine WM/attention under Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched blockade: Without abolish×residual H2H on a Gamo-class WM/attention panel with an atomoxetine arm, separate NET-mechanism LITERATURE and phenotype/tool LITERATURE cannot show net-insufficiency as a residual-positive kill.
2. Remove verified abolish gate (Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched blockade abolishing NET-class attribution) plus atomoxetine-alone comparator: Without verified NET-class abolish and atomoxetine-alone comparator under the same condition, residual atomoxetine is just 'another catecholamine agent under nonspecific challenge,' not an assumption-kill of NET-class sufficiency.
3. Remove N15≠N25 through N24≠N25 discipline and related constraints: Treating N15–N24 residuals as NET abolish, Bymaster mechanism as residual-under-abolish, Xu/Gamo/Michelson phenotype as residual H2H, or Gamo idazoxan as NET abolish would invent an H2H result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refute Condition and Ask-a-Human
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (or NHP Gamo-class) WM/attention panel, under Slc6a2 genetic LOF or NET-matched blockade that abolishes NET-class attribution, residual atomoxetine WM/attention phenotype falls below 50% of atomoxetine-alone — so NET-class sufficiency for the atomoxetine phenotype survives and net-insufficiency fails — when abolish-gate, atomoxetine-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts are ruled out.
Ask a human: Lock acute/subacute rodent (or NHP Gamo-class) WM/attention assay identity, NET-class attribution abolish gate under Slc6a2 LOF or named NET-matched blockade, atomoxetine-alone comparator, and optional cell/SPR/NET occupancy overlay only after abolish×residual locks. Do not treat N15–N24 as proof. No dosing. NOT MB/MAOI. orthosteric_drift=false. Do not invent residual or genetic necessity kill.

key_findings: N25 is a proposed (NOT_RUN) assumption-kill experiment testing whether atomoxetine retains ≥50% of its WM/attention phenotype when NET (Slc6a2) is genetically knocked out or pharmacologically blocked to abolish NET-class attribution.
No published head-to-head study has scored residual-positive atomoxetine WM/attention under Slc6a2 LOF or NET-matched blockade that abolishes NET-class attribution — the key variable is UNKNOWN.

Four prior-art references provide PARTIAL support: Xu (PMID 10769386) — Slc6a2/NET KO tool; Bymaster (PMID 12431845) — NET-selective mechanism attribution; Gamo (PMID 20855046) — NHP PFC WM phenotype with α2/D1 downstream challenge (α2 ≠ NET); Michelson (PMID 12411225) — ADHD RCT phenotype. None includes a residual-under-NET-abolish arm.
Gamo idazoxan×atomoxetine is α2-downstream adjacent, NOT a NET abolish condition — explicitly flagged as a non-match for N25.
DAT-KO×atomoxetine (Ptukha, PMID 36291693) is a NON-MATCH for N25 (DAT ≠ NET).
AMPT catecholamine depletion (N22) ≠ NET LOF; α2-antagonism (N23) ≠ NET abolish — these prior series experiments do not settle N25.

Competing caveats: abolish condition may fail to kill NET-class attribution; atomoxetine-alone may be null; study may be underpowered; assay-identity mismatch — all leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.
Estimated kill cost tier: 1; time to refute: 4 weeks; execution status: NOT_RUN.

Refute condition: residual atomoxetine WM/attention phenotype <50% of atomoxetine-alone under verified NET-class abolish, ruling out abolish-gate failure, null atomoxetine-alone, underpowering, and assay mismatch.
IP class: net-insufficiency; vault hold: no; FTO status: UNKNOWN.
